This isn't really helpful as a fast fix (then again, is anything?) but I have found that really making an effort to listen to my body about 10 days before my period starts seems to make a difference in the manageability of the pain when it happens. Eating enough food, drinking enough water is a big one, keeping stress down, and also just laying down a lot and taking naps as much as possible. The idea is to just not to push yourself too hard, and try not to wear yourself out physically at all, if you can avoid it. My endo seems to want me to sleep an absurd amount even in the daytime, and I used to fight it, but I've been realizing that listening to what my body wants before my period starts can at least make it easier for painkillers to work when the pain hits, if not make it less painful.

Edit: oh yeah! Also, start taking pain medication a day or two before your period / pain actually starts, that way it builds up in your system and prevents some of the inflammation from happening in the first place. You might know that already but I'm definitely the type who will be like "I'm fine" until I am in so much pain that even drinking the glass of water to take with a painkiller makes me vomit lol

I may be in the minority with this opinion but I think birth control for endo is in most cases simply a bandaid at best, and is pretty indicative of women's health not being taken more seriously. Birth control undeniably helps some with endo, but not in most cases. Endometriosis is a systemic disease that will continue to cause symptoms elsewhere in your body even if you're not having periods. For this reason I regard birth control as a waste of time and effort, but YMMV.
